subject: Recap: Ava Health demo — criteria, gaps & proposed tests
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@avahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Ava Health demo — criteria, gaps & proposed tests

Hi Sarah — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track items:  

1) Confirmed pain & goals
- Pain: bursty patient-facing inference at low per-request latency (95p < 250ms) and predictable cost per 1M tokens.
- Goal: baseline POC with 3 endpoints (summarization, triage-scoring, embeddings for retrieval) that hits latency SLO and runs in your VPC.

2) Decision criteria (as discussed)
- Latency under realistic concurrency (50-100 concurrent sessions)
- Cost per token / steady-state throughput
- Security: VPC + KMS integration + audit logs
- Feature parity: streaming + function-like structured output for triage pipeline

3) Open questions / gaps from our side
- Data residency requirement for audit logs (you mentioned EU for a subset) — need exact retention window.
- Procurement: target contract start date and billing cadence.

4) Proposed tests for the bakeoff (owners & timeframe)
- A: Latency stress run (50 concurrent sessions, 2-min steady state) — Owner: Aditya (we can run in your staging VPC). Target: by 2027-05-14.
- B: Token-cost comparison using your triage prompt set (1000 requests/day simulation) — Owner: Camila/Marissa. Target: 2027-05-16.
- C: Failover & regional routing test (us-east <-> us-west) — Owner: Redwood infra. Target: 2027-05-18.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx (attachment: spreadsheet) and an initial MVP runtime config (we'll attach YAML after infra alignment). Link to drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-bakeoff-docs

Can you confirm the targets above and whether procurement should be looped in on the latency test scheduling? If you want, we can produce an abbreviated mutual action plan for sign-off.

Thanks — looking forward to moving to an initial POC.

—
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
(attachment: redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx)

Subject: Re: Recap: Ava Health demo — criteria, gaps & proposed tests

Camila — thanks for the clear summary. Quick notes:  

- Confirmed: latency and cost are the primary gating criteria for our clinical triage rollout. 95p < 250ms is what our product team will expect for the first cohort.
- Procurement: they want an estimated pricing band and contract length options (12/24/36). I copied them here.
- Security: we do require EU residency for logs tied to EU patients; for the initial POC we can scope to US-only test data, but will need a plan for EU audit logs in the contract.

Two asks:  
1) Can you confirm Redwood supports VPC + customer KMS today or is that only in Private deployments?
2) For the latency stress run, we prefer the window 2027-05-13 or 2027-05-14 in the morning PT. Can Aditya confirm availability?

Appreciate the matrix. Evan and I will review and get back with procurement comments by EOD Thursday.

—
Sarah Connors

Date: 2027-05-10T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Competitive snapshot + recommended verification tests (adds)

Adding a quick competitive lens so the POC focuses on differentiators we expect to matter in the decision:  

Snapshot (short):
- Vendor A: very low-latency claims but higher token cost; limited VPC options without dedicated onboarding.
- Vendor B: cheaper for embeddings but less mature streaming and function-output support.
- Redwood: mid-cost, strong streaming & KV cache controls, built-in routing/fallback which helps SLA.

Additional recommended verification tests (proposed owners):
- Token-cost delta test: run identical prompt set across Vendor A/B/Redwood for 10k tokens and measure end-to-end cost & prompt-normalized quality. Owner: Marissa. Target: 2027-05-16.
- Structured output fidelity test: sample triage prompts with function-like outputs, measure parsing failure rate. Owner: Camila. Target: 2027-05-15.
- Regional failover verification (adds to Camila/Aditya's latency run): fail the primary region and confirm routing fallback under pressure. Owner: Aditya. Target: 2027-05-18.

Hypotheses we want to validate:
- Redwood's KV caching will reduce per-token cost in the triage flow by >20% in steady state.
- Competitor A will meet p95 but will spike more often under sustained bursts.

I'll prepare a short one-pager for the exec readout (RDW-AVA-2027-042) and can join the latency window to narrate results.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
